grammar.practice: codetry — naming IS architecture (distinct from code-poetry)
grammar.thunder: there is no shortage of problems, but when we look for solutions it all becomes a little easier

principles.name: one bounded thing you can point at
principles.statement: A primitive names one bounded system with one specific job. The name holds across every zone, every season, every personnel rotation. It works from day one — empty and full, built and forming. The name is not a category label; it is the system itself.
principles.workedExample: Saltbox — named for the cold-climate vernacular house whose asymmetric roof and thick north wall were the only way a house survived a boreal winter. The form is the function. Every beam carries weight. A codetry app is named the same way: the name is the design spec, and changing it changes the structure underneath.

principles.name: the name has to hold both states
principles.statement: When a system has both a slow side (always-on practice) and a fast side (active event), the name has to do both jobs in one word, or the system will fork into two systems with two cultures.
principles.workedExample: The Standby — the umbrella name had to hold both the always-on shelf (preparation, standby stock, the watch as a posture) and the active event (a call, an active rung, a debrief). Splitting into two names — say, *the Pantry* for the slow side and *the Call* for the fast side — would have produced two systems with two cultures. One word, two states.

principles.name: the name has to hold both sides
principles.statement: When a system has language that has to live in two contexts that hold different vocabularies as legitimate, the umbrella name has to fit both contexts in one word, or the system will pick a dialect and lose the other room.
principles.workedExample: The Gate — the umbrella name had to hold both the *bright side* (the constellation's own dialect: neighbour, channel, the books, standby stock) and *the systems* (the outside world's dialect: resident, bank account, financial statements, inventory reserves). Splitting into two names — say, *Translator* for the bright-to-systems direction and *Importer* for the systems-to-bright direction — would have produced two pipes and no posture, with no record that both names exist for the same thing. One word, two contexts.

constellationWidePrimitives.name: The Standby
constellationWidePrimitives.summary: The umbrella system + always-on state for *temporary centralized disruptions* — drought, fire, smoke, flood, ice, power, water, freight, payment systems, pandemic, evacuation, AGM-postponed, key-person-down. One name that holds both the slow side (always-on preparation) and the fast side (active event).
constellationWidePrimitives.hostZoneRationale: Hosted in Zone 3 (community production) because that is where centralized disruptions are felt collectively. The co-op shelf, the producer pipeline, the orders ledger are where the absence of freight, power, or staff lands first. Read by every zone.

vocabulary.role: a specific active event (a fire call, a flood call, a freight call)
the active-monitoring posture between advisory and active — the sub-noun for the act of watching a developing situation
the physical/operational reserves the always-on side maintains
the after-action synthesis once a call has stood down
the class of event the Standby is for — a temporary loss or strain of a centralized system the community depends on

severityLadder.meaning: something is forming on the horizon; no posture change required, but the watch is informed
preparation is sleeved in; standby stock is verified; envelopes ready to flex
a call is open; the system is responding; envelopes and rosters have flipped
the call is closed; debrief opens; standby stock is replenished

subShelves.name: The Common Pantry
subShelves.role: the food/supply sub-noun — the literal shelf inside the Standby that holds staples, water, fuel, medicine. Sub-noun, not replacement.

subShelves.name: The Watch
subShelves.role: the active-monitoring sub-noun — the posture and the people doing the watching during advisory/standby rungs. Sub-noun, not replacement.

rejectedAlternatives.name: The Common Pantry (as the umbrella name)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Holds the slow side beautifully (a pantry is by definition always-on) but cannot hold an active fire call, an evacuation, or a payment-systems outage without straining the metaphor. A pantry is what you keep; the Standby is also what you do. The Pantry sits *inside* the Standby as the food/supply sub-shelf.

rejectedAlternatives.name: The Watch (as the umbrella name)
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Holds the active-monitoring posture (the watch is active by definition) but cannot hold the slow shelf of standby stock without bending into something that sounds like a permanent vigil. The Watch sits *inside* the Standby as the active-monitoring sub-noun.

constellationWidePrimitives.scope: naming and filing only — no UI surface for tracking calls, watches, or debriefs is built on this pass. Future task once the vocabulary has been used in the field.

constellationWidePrimitives.name: The Gate
constellationWidePrimitives.summary: A calm passage between the bright side and the systems. The umbrella system + posture for *passing language across institutional boundaries* — codetry vocabulary going out to a regulator, banker, funder, lawyer, or other legacy-world counterparty; their vocabulary coming back in. Holds both sides without flattening either: the founder/practitioner keeps the original noun, the counterparty receives the dialect they can act on, and the gate logs the substitution so the translation stays auditable.
constellationWidePrimitives.hostZoneRationale: Hosted in Zone 3 (community production) because that is where the community meets the legacy world — the co-op invoices a wholesaler, the producer signs a band council resolution, the Headwaters bookkeeper files with CRA. Sibling to The Standby (also Z3-hosted): both umbrella systems operate at the boundary where centralized systems and the community-controlled side touch. Read by every zone whose work has to leave the constellation in writing.

vocabulary.role: the codetry-vocabulary side; the constellation's own dialect
the outside world's side; the systems dialect (regulators, bankers, funders, lawyers, generic SaaS English)
a registered correspondence between a bright-side term and its systems-side equivalent (e.g. neighbour → resident, send → remit, fee → service charge, money → funds)
a single instance of a mapping being applied to a piece of crossing language
the domain a mapping belongs to (Pragmatism, Politics, Regulations, Privacy, Banking, …); each category is a sub-shelf inside the Gate
a piece of language that has passed through the Gate in either direction; the auditable record of what crossed and what changed
the metaphor doing the load — selectively permeable, alive, not a wall and not a wide-open door; the gate does work without picking a side

severityLadder.meaning: language has been written but not run past the Gate yet; no posture change required
the Gate is reading the language; mappings are being proposed; the founder is in the loop
the language has crossed; substitutions are logged; the translation is part of the record
the Gate declined to translate — usually because the bright-side noun has no honest systems-side equivalent and forcing one would lose the meaning the founder is trying to keep

subShelves.name: Mappings
subShelves.role: the registered correspondences that the Gate carries — the dictionary side. Sub-noun, not replacement: a Mapping is what the Gate knows; the Gate is also what it does with what it knows.

subShelves.name: Substitutions
subShelves.role: the applied-instance ledger — every time a mapping has been used, who used it, on what document, in which direction. Sub-noun, not replacement: substitutions are the Gate's history; the Gate is also its present.

subShelves.name: Categories
subShelves.role: the domain shelves the mappings live on (Pragmatism, Politics, Regulations, Privacy, Banking, …). Sub-noun, not replacement: a category is where a mapping is filed; the Gate is the building all the categories sit in.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Translator
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Holds the directional work but flattens the gate's posture into pure transaction — a translator processes; a gate decides whether to. Strips the calm-passage feel out of the metaphor.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Filter
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Implies the Gate's job is to remove or block, which mis-frames the work — the Gate doesn't subtract, it relabels in flight while keeping both names on file. A filter chooses what gets through; the Gate chooses what the through-language is called on each side.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Censor
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Carries punitive weight the metaphor refuses; the Gate is collaborative with the founder, not adversarial. A censor decides for you; the Gate proposes and lets the founder confirm.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Glossary
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Holds the dictionary side (Mappings) beautifully but cannot hold the active posture of substituting in real documents, the ledger of past substitutions, or the refused-translation rung. A glossary is what you keep on a shelf; the Gate is the shelf plus the room plus the work happening in it.

constellationWidePrimitives.scope: in-repo runnable surface lives at /gate inside artifacts/headwaters-books — a sibling route to /standby that reads this manifest verbatim for vocabulary, severity ladder (draft/under-review/cleared/refused), sub-shelves, and rejected alternatives, lets a real bright-side ↔ systems substitution be entered with category and direction, and persists the substitution ledger in the browser so it survives reload. glossary.rationale: Two distinct primitives both named with the bare word 'cost'. They live in different artifacts, with different shapes, storage layers, and audiences. Today the artifacts don't cross-reference each other, so the bare word works in its own context. The moment they do (e.g. a future bridge that posts approved registry figures into Cost Centres), a reader holding both will silently fuse them. This entry heads that off on paper before the first cross-reference site needs it; the convention is cheap now and a schema-level rename later.

primitives.name: Headwaters Books cost centre
primitives.shape: named bookkeeping bucket where real expenses land for tracking and reporting (code, name, parentEntity, owner, isActive)
primitives.storageLayer: server-backed (Postgres via Drizzle, behind the API)
primitives.verb: post — a real expense lands in a cost centre

primitives.name: Practitioner cost-registry entry
primitives.shape: canonical planned figure with id, value, narrative, and per-entry status (pending review / approved / edited) — the source-of-truth dictionary the slides resolve against via resolveCost()
primitives.storageLayer: browser localStorage under 'pop:v1' (no backend, no auth)
primitives.audience: the practitioner walking the cost review
primitives.verb: approve / edit — a planned figure changes status

glossary.convention: When both appear in the same surface (a doc, a slide, a wiring layer), use the long forms — 'Practitioner cost-registry entry' and 'Headwaters Books cost centre' — never the bare word 'cost'. Within a single artifact's interior copy, the short form is fine; the long form is the cross-reference contract.

drift.trigger: the first wiring that crosses the artifact boundary (e.g. posting an approved cost-registry figure into a Headwaters Books cost centre)
drift.auditEntry: Headwaters Books group · 'cost centre vs. cost registry (cross-artifact name collision)' on /practitioner-operating-plan/codetry-test

zones.opening:
Sitting on the deck with the morning sun and a cup of black coffee. Getting cold, but that's nothing new. Watching the children play outside — and then all of a sudden there's a moment. There's always a beautiful moment to capture. A moment where we wonder: will this ever cross my mind again? Will they remember? Saltbox is the reminder of the things that are true and unshakeable. The sunny moments that make the boreal winters worth bearing. The spring days when the outdoors is the parent and we can just enjoy documenting the ride.

The no-scoring rule comes from this: a measure of a fish's worth cannot be how well it can climb a tree. We each have our individual strengths, and when channeled, those strengths allow a waterfall of value that was never dammed. With a proper saltbox, the children grow brave in their own time — and the dams that don't need breaking down the line are the fruit of that patience.

Zone 0 holds both the family on the land and the elder in the care home. They are just homes in different stages, and they deserve the same value placed on their life stage.
zones.inlinePrompt: What moment from this week would you regret losing? Name it before the day ends.
reflections: What are the things that are true and unshakeable in your household right now?
Where are you measuring a fish by how well it climbs a tree?
What would it look like to let someone grow brave in their own time instead of pushing the pace?
What were you handed by the generations before you in this household — and what are you handing forward to the ones who will sit in this kitchen after you?
What does this household look like three generations from now — and is anything you are building today pointed at that?

zones.careCircleDesignPrinciples: Zone 1 care circle design principles (from Mama Support Hub, May 2026): (1) Language is the circle — task-tracker language quietly changes how people relate to showing up. Needs/Moments/I've got it/Someone's on it are not cosmetic; they are the architecture. (2) The ask dissolves when it is answered — no permanent audit log of care. The record that the circle existed is enough; what was needed and by whom is not the system's to keep. (3) Dissolution is the organizer's act of stewardship — not the system's automatic action, not the supported person's burden. What survives dissolution: the circle's name (first name only, surname cleared), date range, member count, dissolved flag. What goes: situation, address, logistics, slot content, comments, activity, memories (export-then-delete offered before dissolution). (4) Impact sections measure the wrong thing — quantifying care as productivity output (14 tasks completed) tells the circle nothing about whether the person felt held. Remove without replacement. (5) Invite links create closed circles by architecture — no open registration into a care circle is the correct posture, regardless of link expiry enforcement.

workedExamples.name: Eave
workedExamples.rule: the eave is the first shelter outward from the household — the immediate circle of trust that catches what the household cannot hold alone. Rename to 'Network' and you lose the constraint that this zone is built on invitation, not open access; every downstream zone flows from that boundary being held.

workedExamples.name: Buckets
workedExamples.rule: envelope categories. You can only pour from one bucket into another; never summon water from nothing. Every transfer is a literal redistribution. Rename to 'Categories' and the UI starts quietly suggesting balances can grow by clicking. Per Test 005, 'cistern' was retired in favour of Bucket — the Earn surface had been calling savings envelopes 'cisterns' in violation of the locked Eave word map.

workedExamples.name: XRP Spring
workedExamples.rule: savings, defined as free XRP above the 10-XRP network reserve. A spring upwells from below the reserve floor; the user sees what's pooled above the rock. The new six-stage bamboo growth scene (just shipped, #793) extends the metaphor from data model into artwork — same constraint, now visible.

workedExamples.name: Drip Harvester
workedExamples.rule: two senses, both held by Test 008's resolution. As a noun: an earner wallet that holds RLUSD before it is parked in a Lake — the station between Reservoir and Private Lake on the Earn flow ribbon. As a verb: the move that drips Lake earnings into a Bucket once a sweep threshold is reached. The verb 'harvest' carries patience and seasonality; 'Auto-Compound' would have erased both.

workedExamples.name: Community Well
workedExamples.rule: monthly pooled tips that round-distribute to community proposals. A well everyone draws from and contributes to; the monthly snapshot/round cycle is the well refilling.

workedExamples.name: Giving Well
workedExamples.rule: user-to-user tip pool for charitable giving. Same well metaphor at the household scale.

workedExamples.name: Surplus Pool
workedExamples.rule: where Payday overflow goes once envelopes are full. Pool, not 'extra savings account' — water seeking level. (In flight: #794)

workedExamples.name: Payday Planner
workedExamples.rule: the moment the spring refills. Allocation flow follows water's priority order: must-pay buckets first, then comfort buckets, then Surplus Pool, then giving.

workedExamples.name: Rainfall
workedExamples.rule: income arriving this payday — paycheck plus side gig combined, before anything is taken out. The act of arriving, not the leftover; the leftover is the Reservoir.

workedExamples.name: Siphon
workedExamples.rule: auto-bills drawn out of the rainfall before it reaches the Reservoir. The locked verb for money leaving rainfall before it reaches the wallet — replaces 'bank' wherever it had crept in (Test 001 Sighting 1).

workedExamples.name: Reservoir
workedExamples.rule: the stablecoin wallet — what's left after the Siphon. The locked noun for the wallet itself; the field name in code is `reservoirLabel`, no longer `masterBucketLabel`. The wallet/XRP-swap chip honours this lock end-to-end after Tests 009 and 010.

workedExamples.name: Channel (verb)
workedExamples.rule: distributing the Reservoir into named Buckets — the act of 'every drop into a bucket'. Reserved for Reservoir → Bucket only; the Bridge sheet uses 'Bridge' for above-cap transfers, the Drainage lesson uses 'Drainage' for debt payoff, and the Drip Harvester uses 'drip' for Lake → Bucket.

workedExamples.name: Cloud Cover
workedExamples.rule: compound interest — the weather that keeps producing rain. Separated from the vehicle (Glacier) where it happens; the lesson formerly called 'Compound Rainfall' was re-named to introduce both nouns explicitly.

workedExamples.name: Rain Barrel
workedExamples.rule: emergency fund — the short-term reserve for surprises. The first layer of the Aquifer ladder; the daily drops about not draining the emergency fund were re-pointed from 'Reservoir' to 'Rain Barrel' to honour Test 002's lock.

workedExamples.name: Aquifer
workedExamples.rule: long-term savings — the deep reserve that fills slowly. The 3–6 month layer of the savings ladder; replaces 'Reservoir' wherever the lessons were using it for long-term savings.

workedExamples.name: Glacier
workedExamples.rule: tax-advantaged accounts (RRSP, TFSA) — savings the tax authority leaves alone. The vehicle Cloud Cover compounds inside; named explicitly so compounding (the weather) is no longer conflated with where it happens (the vehicle).

workedExamples.name: Watershed
workedExamples.rule: diversified income streams — one fragile stream becomes many resilient ones. Distinct from the former xBuckets product name 'Watershed' (still active at the URL/storage layer); here the noun refers to multiple income streams the household draws from. 'Three is a Watershed' replaces 'Three is a reservoir' across the side-income card and daily drops.

workedExamples.name: Bridge (verb)
workedExamples.rule: above-tap-cap transfers — the Abundance Bridge sheet. The locked verb for transfers that exceed the daily cap; the Bridge sheet was rewritten to use 'Bridge this rainfall' / 'Bridge this →' / 'Bridged across' instead of 'Channel', preserving Channel for Reservoir → Bucket only.

workedExamples.name: Public Lake
workedExamples.rule: regulated / credit-union yield product — the advisor-mode Earn destination. Half of the Park-rename pair (Public Park / Private Park were renamed to Public Lake / Private Lake by Task #849 so the destination sits cleanly inside the watershed metaphor).

workedExamples.name: Private Lake
workedExamples.rule: DeFi liquidity pool — the enthusiast-mode Earn destination, self-custody. The Earn flow ribbon's third station after Reservoir and Drip Harvester; replaces 'AMM pool' / 'liquidity pool' on every user-facing surface (Test 005).

workedExamples.name: Lake current
workedExamples.rule: the small fee paid into a Public/Private Lake each time a swap flows through it; the Drip Harvester's earnings are its share of those currents. Renamed from 'Park toll' by Task #849; the metaphor is that water flows through channels, collects in your Lake, and Currents from the Lake drip back into your Buckets.

workedExamples.name: Fill (verb)
workedExamples.rule: the act of putting idle RLUSD into a Lake. Renamed from 'park' by Task #849 — the Earn surface used 'park' as the verb for moving RLUSD into an LP; 'fill' brings the verb inside the water register and removes the last instance of 'park' from any Eave surface (decision logged in Test 002, Task #851).

workedExamples.name: Drainage
workedExamples.rule: debt payoff — the opposite move from Channel. The locked noun for paying down debt; the lesson formerly called 'Debt Channeling' was renamed 'Debt Drainage' so 'Channel' could be reserved for Reservoir → Bucket only (Test 002).

workedExamples.name: Park toll
workedExamples.rule: the swap fee a Park collects when someone exchanges through it; the Drip Harvester's earnings are its share of those tolls. Coined in Test 005 as the new noun replacing 'fee per swap' / 'trading fees' on the Earn surface — later renamed to 'Lake current' by Task #849 when the Park metaphor itself was renamed to Lake. Recorded here as the original sanctioned noun from Test 005's vocabulary sweep.

workedExamples.name: Scaffolding pretending to be engine
workedExamples.rule: Roughly 600 lines of procedural-music machinery — kick/snare scheduler, synth functions, chord timeline, LFO, music bus, per-scene chord-morph effect — sat behind ENABLE_PROCEDURAL_MUSIC = false for months in the Headwaters promo video's audio file, shaping how the file read and what future contributors thought the system did. Named as 'feature behind a flag' it was untouchable; named honestly as scaffolding pretending to be engine, it could be deleted, and ambient-audio.ts collapsed from 933 lines to ~330 with no change in runtime behavior. A flag that has been off long enough to forget why it was added is not a feature toggle — it is a name lying about the system's intent, and the honest move is to delete it.

zones.opening:
The word "budget" evokes restriction, tightening. "Watershed" invokes flow, abundance. That difference is not cosmetic — it changes what the person holding the tool believes is possible before they touch a single number.

The Siphon is the bill that leaves before you see the money. But the siphon isn't permanent. You choose the size of it. You can reduce those bills, downgrade the lifestyle, make pivots. You ultimately control it — which is the opposite of what the word "expense" implies.

zones.opening:
"Founder" feels odd. You don't found a community — you practice within it. You join to help. You have the phone calls, take the actions, practice listening. We practice these things because we know we need to. Crafting all day is what makes life that extra bit sweeter.

This is not a founder's dashboard. It is a practitioner's workbench — the place where the week is planned, the costs are walked, and the work is kept honest against what was said it would be.

workedExamples.name: 'Today I…' verbs as routing primitive
workedExamples.rule: the library front door isn't a menu of features; it's a shelf of verbs the member picks based on what today asks for (Today I cook & preserve / gather / order / learn / trade / help). workedExamples.rule: audience-aware shelves of 8–12 themed stacks. Stacks = chapters, audience choice = which book. Visual recently caught up to metaphor — tiles read as printed recipe cards on a photo. Two-column on phones (a paired spread), three-column on desktop.

workedExamples.name: Treasurer Calm Monthly Journey
workedExamples.rule: 'Calm' is the contract, not a vibe. Confidence meter + per-treasurer lookahead preference (off / 1 / 2 / 3 days) + 14-day snooze-expiry outline + email digest + in-app banner. Treasurers plan ahead instead of reacting.

workedExamples.name: Dues snooze as primary verb
workedExamples.rule: treasurers don't 'defer' or 'pause' a dues line — they snooze it, and the system auto-wakes them with a digest tied to (recipient, lineItem, snoozedUntil). The verb dictates the behavior (something will wake you), not the other way around.

workedExamples.name: Stuck Board
workedExamples.rule: cross-domain aggregator at /admin/stuck and /board-hub/stuck. Pulls aging items from member onboarding, producer pipeline, outstanding dues, partner/grant sync errors, open grants, and marketplace seller replies into one owner-tagged view with last-touch timestamps. The name is the spec: things get stuck → the board surfaces them.

workedExamples.name: Producer Playbook
workedExamples.rule: sequenced markdown chapters producers work through, surfaced as list/detail with mailto CTAs back to the co-op. Playbook = ordered plays, not a wiki.

workedExamples.name: NOHFC Grow Application Workspace
workedExamples.rule: single-grant focused workspace at /applications/nohfc-grow-stream (lives in the Grants Finder artifact). Five tabs (eligibility, sections, budget, attachments, submission packet), deadline countdown, one-click switch to July 31 intake on a not-eligible verdict. workedExamples.rule: signed-out visitors choose household vs producer; the choice persists in localStorage (807.audience.v1) and changes which library, which CTAs, and which dashboard cards render. One pivot, two products.

Centralized disruptions (drought, fire, smoke, flood, ice, power, water, freight, payment systems, pandemic, evacuation, AGM-postponed, key-person-down) are felt collectively here first — at the co-op shelf, the producer pipeline, the orders ledger. Call history is the record kept here; standby stock is the inventory primitive; The Common Pantry is the food/supply sub-shelf; The Watch is the active-monitoring sub-noun.
zones.opening:
Treasurer is the job nobody wants. Some try and fail; a few do well. It is a big commitment for a volunteer organization, and this generation does not have the same bookkeeping skills that the last one had. Nobody wants to step up because they do not want to mess up.

The answer is not to lower the standard — it is to make the job fail-safe, stress-free, and easy as pie for the people willing to take it on. Calm is the contract. The name is not a vibe; it is a promise the system makes to the person who was brave enough to say yes.

Regen beef in NWO, for example: a freight call hits the abattoir's outbound packed weights before it hits anything else; a power call hits cold storage; a key-person call hits Jude herself. zones.opening:
It is not just the spreadsheet and the phone call. It is the Facebook comments, the Instagram comments, the Facebook messages, the marketplace comments, the email, the voicemail, the text message, the in-person conversation, the invoice. One person has to touch it all — because it is the only way the ball of yarn will not unravel.

The producers running these operations are not failing for lack of effort. They are failing for lack of capacity. If they had the capacity to systematize, they could find the efficiencies needed for real growth. That is the job this zone exists to do.

The word they use is not "regenerative." It is grass finished. Grazing. Fodder fed. The work names itself in what it produces and how it is done.

What would this sector look like if every decision made in it for the last 175 years had been made with the seventh generation in mind — and how far is today from that?

codetryObservations: Chapter IDs are the schema enum: headwaters | tributaries | confluence | burst | delta. The display labels swapped to the rescue-at-sea family (Compass / Cast Off / Breakers / Adrift / Aboard) during the rebrand, but the IDs stayed. The bones were the metaphor — we changed the skin and the bones held.
Take chapter classification is keyword-scored against those IDs in pure code (computeChapterHint). The English words drive the bucket assignment; the metaphor is the type system.
Storage keys preserve the original watershed namespace (watershed:takes:v1, watershed:dedication:*) on purpose — the metaphor evolves at the prose layer; the ground at the data layer holds.
Channel output mirrors the constellation itself — Zone 5's app produces Zone-0-through-5 reads of the user's own life. The app teaches the meta-pattern by being it.
Shallows handles are derived deterministically from (sessionToken, postId), with reply-handle collisions resolved per-thread. Pseudonymity-as-architecture, not as policy.

workedExamples.rule: The Zone 5 app was deployed as watershed.replit.app before The Margin existed as a zone name. When the rename happened, it touched display strings, prose, and the Forge prompt — not chapter IDs, storage keys, or schema. The codetry test: change the name, did the structure survive? Yes — because the structure was the metaphor underneath the name. The URL stayed watershed.replit.app; the concept Watershed moved to Zone 1 where it always belonged.

zones.opening:
A dam day is a day without rhyme or reason — where a spark was lit and a fire burst forth. It may be a creative hyperfocus, or a day that required a shift of energy that no constellation can contain. Dam days are fleeting. But there are gems worth harnessing in them — they may just be covered in muck.

The Shallows is where you clean them off. Not every take becomes something. But the practice of catching it before it disappears is the whole discipline.

Headwaters ≠ Watershed ≠ xBuckets (former names of Z1; current canonical name is Headwaters; note Z5 still uses 'Watershed' at URL/storage layer). Snooze ≠ defer/pause (the verb commits the system to wake you). Borrow ≠ rent (kitchen access — naming carries policy). Stuck ≠ overdue (Stuck Board is a cross-domain aging-item aggregator, not a deadline list). Playbook ≠ wiki (ordered plays, not browsable info). Calm ≠ comfortable/easy (treasurer monthly-journey contract). Share split ≠ cut sheet management (the math AFTER the kill, not the spec at booking — Z4 v0.1 centerpiece). Byproduct ≠ feature (OMAFRA log falls out for free, doesn't get its own ledger). Loop ≠ three features (estimate → actual → variance read together). Take ≠ Note ≠ Entry ≠ Moment (Z5 Take is a fragment for channel-or-Forge; Saltbox Moment is a keepsake; both deliberately resist 'note'/'entry' flattening). Channel ≠ Tag ≠ Categorize (Z5's Channel produces a structured 6-zone read of the user's life, not a label).
